brief: Squat masonry silo of the early 1900s dairy era, about 16 ft across and 30 ft high, built of rough granite rubble with a thin weathered stucco skin, roofless, with a stack of rectangular door openings one above another up one side (a few rotted door boards left) and a small rim ledge at the top. Long abandoned: saplings and brush have grown up around it so it stands in a young woodlot at the edge of the farmyard. (Stone masonry; nearest vocabulary type is brick.)
